title: Accursed Spectre (reaction)
html:
See also: Accursed Spectre (passive feature)
Accursed Spectre is a reaction granted to The Hexblade warlocks that allows them to raise a spectre from a fallen enemy cursed by  Hexblade's Curse.

Description

Raise an Accursed Spectre from the soul of a fallen cursed target to fight by your side. The size of the fallen creature will determine whether you raise a  Feeble Spectre,  Mundane Spectre, or  Primordial Spectre.

Doesn't work with constructs, elementals, oozes, plants, or undead.

How to learn

Classes:
  • Class level 6: The Hexblade

Notes

  • It is not stated anywhere, but spectres get  temporary hit points equal to half the summoners level and deal bonus damage equal to the summoner's Charisma modifier.
  • This feature cannot be used on summoned creatures, either allied or enemy.
  • It also cannot be used on any creature with an effect like  Death Ward which revives the creature after dropping to 0 hit points. This is true even after the condition is expended.
  • Accursed Spectres are not traditional summons; they cannot be directly controlled by the player and they are immobile. However, they can teleport to creatures hit by the warlock's  Hexed Weapon and take an immediately attack through their  Right Behind You reaction. This allows for a degree of indirect control over the spectre.
  • Multiple spectres can be summoned simultaneously. Unlike most other summoning abilities, conjuring a new spectre does not unsummon the existing one.
  • Spectres are immune to the  Madness effect from the  Abyss Beckoners gloves.

Bugs

  • The description does not state it, but this cannot be used on undead.
  • Creatures killed by  Cull the Weak will not trigger this reaction.
  • The CharacterStats for this summoned creature does not correctly have the proper DifficultyStatuses set, and as a result the creature loses 30% HP from the Explorer difficulty modifier as if it were a hostile NPC.
  • This reaction cannot be used while affected by  Starry Form or when  Disguised.
